In <s>anumāna</s> (inference), however, that [commentary] is grounded, for the refutation of all objections, because through it the true nature of reality, as it is and not perverted,
Because even for that which has a clear appearance, being non-conceptual, [such appearance] is possible even in cognitions such as seeing double moons and the like —

this is not so for <s>anumāna</s> (inference): in its semblances, the ascertained triple characteristic is impossible — therefore, through the purity of the causal conditions of actual <s>anumāna</s> (inference)

children.text: णैव प्रत्यक्षस्य प्रामाण्यं निश्‍चेयं । यद्यप्यान्ये(?)षितमात्रं यथावस्तु प्रवर्त्तते
children.translated_text: alone, the validity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is to be ascertained. Even if <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), [when] merely(?), operates in accordance with the object,
that too, having been employed in practice repeatedly, having its object-form discerned through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance),
is known to be veridical — and this is preceded by <s>anumāna</s> (inference), since <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> are of the nature of <s>anumāna</s>. And it is observed
that <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) arising from the culmination of practice is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), like cognition of gems, silver, and so forth — such

children.text: विधतत्स्वत एव प्रमाणं भ्रान्तिनिमित्तस्याभ्यासेनैव निराकृतत्वात् । अन्यथा
children.translated_text: is intrinsically a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because the cause of error has been eliminated through practice itself. Otherwise,

children.text: कथं लिङ्गज्ञानं प्रमाणं स्यात् । यत्र तु क्‍वचिद्विषये भ्रान्तिनिमित्तापनयासमर्थन्तत्
children.translated_text: how could <s>liṅgajñāna</s> (inferential cognition from a mark) be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? But where, in some object, one is unable to remove the cause of error, there

children.text: तत्रानुमानानिश्‍चय इति तत्पूर्वमुक्‍तं । नन्वनुमानमपि प्रत्यक्षपूर्वमेव नायन्‍नियमो
children.translated_text: there is uncertainty of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — this has been stated earlier. Now, <s>anumāna</s> too is indeed preceded by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) — this is not a fixed rule,

children.text: व्याप्‍तेरनुमानेन निश्‍चयात् । न हि व्याप्‍तिर्व्यापकस्य तत्र भाव एव । व्याप्यस्य
children.translated_text: because <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is ascertained by <s>anumāna</s>. For <s>vyāpti</s> is not [merely] the presence of the pervader in that [locus]. Of the pervaded,

children.text: वा तत्रैव भाव इत्ययं नियमोऽध्यक्षेणेक्षते । लिङ्गमपि गृहीतसम्बन्धेनैव पुंसा
children.translated_text: or its presence only there — this restriction is not perceived by direct perception. The <s>liṅga</s> (mark) too is ascertained by a person only when the relation has been grasped,
and therefore, since it depends on the relation, that too is preceded by <s>anumāna</s> (inference). And at the time of the manifestation of <s>anumāna</s>,

children.text: काले प्रत्यक्षं व्याप्रियते इत्युक्‍तं । न हि प्रत्यक्षप्रतिभासवत् स्वाभासेऽनुमानं सम्भव
children.translated_text: <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) does not operate — this has been stated. For <s>anumāna</s> is not possible in its own semblance in the way that <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) [is possible] in its semblance —
this too has been stated. Therefore, <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is stated first because it establishes the [previously] stated purpose.
Alternatively, that treatise by which the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),
<s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) are defined — that defining treatise is the <s>Tripiṭaka</s> (Three Baskets).
And it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), and having come into being,

children.text: दित्वाल्लक्षणशास्‍त्रं चेति प्रमाणलक्षणशास्‍त्रं भगवत्प्रवचनं न तीर्थिकानामिव शास्‍त्रं
children.translated_text: because it is a defining treatise — <s>pramāṇalakṣaṇaśāstra</s> (treatise defining valid cognition) means the Word of the Blessed One, not like the treatises of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) which are

children.text: विसम्वादकमलक्षणञ्‍च वस्तुस्वरूपस्येति भावः । तथा हि भगवतां वचनं प्रमाणोप
children.translated_text: deceptive and do not define the true nature of things — this is the purport. For indeed the word of the Blessed Ones is endowed with <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition),

children.text: पन्‍नमनित्यादिवस्तुरूपसम्बेद्यकं चाथवा प्रमाणं प्रत्यक्षानुमाने तयोर्लक्षणं भगवतैव
children.translated_text: and makes known the nature of things such as impermanence, etc. — or alternatively, <s>pramāṇa</s> means <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference); their definition has been taught by the Blessed One
himself.
As stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>:
"it is blue"' —
'A person endowed with visual consciousness knows blue, but not
by this, non-conceptual <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) as sensory cognition has been stated.
'One endowed with mental consciousness,

children.text: समङ्गी तु नीलं जानाति नीलमिति त्वि
children.translated_text: however, knows blue, and "it is blue"' —
here, by the first [part], non-conceptual mental

children.text: प्रत्यक्षमुक्‍तं द्वितीयेन तु विकल्पकं मन उक्‍तं । सम्वित्तिस्तु जानातिवचनेनोक्‍ता ।
children.translated_text: <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) has been stated; by the second, however, conceptual mind has been stated. <s>Saṃvitti</s> (self-awareness) has been stated by the expression 'knows.'

children.text: न हि स्वयमप्रकाशमन्यं प्रकाशयति बाह्यप्रकाशवत् विशेषवचनमप्यस्त्यनुभवरूपं
children.translated_text: For that which does not illuminate itself does not illuminate another, unlike an external light — and there is also a specific statement: 'cognition has the nature of experience.'
<s>Yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition) too has been stated therein through the sequence of hearing, reflection, and meditation.
The definition of <s>kāryānumāna</s> (inference from effect), however, is:
'Fire is known by smoke, and water by the crane.
The lineage of a wise <s>bodhisattva</s> is known by signs.'
The definition of <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature as reason) is:
'Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things), having the nature of arising and ceasing.

children.text: उत्पद्य हि निरुध्यन्ते तेषां व्युपशमः सुखमिति ।
children.translated_text: Having arisen, they are destroyed — their cessation is happiness.'

children.text: एतत्प्रमाणं येन शास्यते भगवद्वचनेन तत्प्रमाणलक्षणशासकं वचनं शास्‍त्रं
children.translated_text: That <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) by which [things] are taught — the Word of the Blessed One — that word, the treatise, teaches and defines <s>pramāṇa</s>.
That

children.text: भगवदुक्‍तं प्रमाणलक्षणमाचार्य दि ग्‍ना गे न व्याख्यातं प्र मा ण स मु च्‍च ये नेत्याचा
children.translated_text: definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> stated by the Blessed One has been explained by master <s>Dignāga</s> in the <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s>. Thus, the master's
treatise on the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) that has been explained — its basis is <s>anumāna</s> (inference), [which] in this <s>Vārttika</s>, first
has been established, for the purpose stated — this is the meaning. 'Having arrived at its occasion' — since everywhere the virtuous proceed

children.text: पूर्वकं प्रवर्त्तन्त इति सदाचारानुवृत्यर्थं विघ्‍नोपशमनार्थञ्‍चाचार्येण प्र मा ण स मु
children.translated_text: with a salutation first, for the sake of following good conduct and for the pacification of obstacles, the master composed a verse of salutation to the Blessed One in the <s>Pramāṇa-</s>

children.text: च्‍च ये भगवतो नमस्कारश्‍लोक उक्‍तः । नमस्कारेण हि पुण्योपचयो भवति । स च
children.translated_text: <s>samuccaya</s>. For through salutation there is an accumulation of merit, and that

children.text: पापं निवर्त्तयति विरोधात् । पापञ्‍च निवर्त्तमानं स्वकार्यमपि विघ्‍नं निवर्त्तयतीति
children.translated_text: removes sin, because they are opposed. And sin, when being removed, also removes its own effect, namely obstacles —
thus there is pacification of obstacles. And since <s>anumāna</s> (inference) based on the validity of the Blessed One has been stated immediately after, the explanation
of the salutatory verse arrives at its occasion.

children.text: प्रमाणभूताय जगद्धितैषिणे प्रणम्य शास्‍त्रे सुगताय तायिने ।
children.translated_text: 'Having bowed to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the Protector, who has become a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), who desires the welfare of the world, to that teacher,
for the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), a <s>samuccaya</s> (compendium) will be composed here, unified from what has been dispersed [in his own doctrine].'
<s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s> 1.1
— of this [verse].
Here, the dependence of the property to be proved on the mere existence of that [reason] has been stated — thus this is said to be a <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature [reason]).
There, just as <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) such as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the like illuminates an object not previously apprehended and is useful for human purposes,

children.text: सम्वादकञ्‍च तथा भगवानपि यत्रोत्कृष्‍टः पुरुषार्थः प्रतिबद्धश्‍चतुरार्यंसत्य
children.translated_text: and is also reliable — so too is the Blessed One; the supreme human purpose is connected with the truth

children.text: लक्षणे तत्त्वे तद्विषयं हि ज्ञानमासाद्य मोक्षार्थिनां मोक्षाधिगमात् । तस्य
children.translated_text: characterized by the Four Noble Truths, for through attaining knowledge of that, those seeking liberation achieve liberation. Of that
[truth] not previously apprehended, the Blessed One is the illuminator and the non-deceiver, and no one else — thus, by analogy with <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), he is a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
<s>Bhūta</s> means 'arisen.' The word <s>bhūta</s> is as if for the purpose of denying the others' conception of a permanent <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) who is not born,

children.text: धार्थमिवार्थस्तु सामर्थ्यगत इति न तदर्थमेतदिति वक्ष्यते । प्रमाणञ्‍चासौ भूत
children.translated_text: but the [actual] meaning is understood from the context — it is not for that purpose, as will be explained. 'And he is a <s>pramāṇa</s> and has come into being' —

children.text: श्‍चेति प्रमाणभूतः । तस्मै प्रमाणभूताय प्रणम्येति योज्यम् ।
children.translated_text: thus <s>pramāṇabhūta</s> (one who has become a valid cognition). 'To him, the <s>Pramāṇabhūta</s>, having bowed' — thus it should be construed.

children.text: ननु च प्रणमनक्रियया व्याप्यमानत्वात् द्वितीययात्र भवितव्यं तत्कथं चतुर्थी
न चेयं नमः शब्दयोगे युज्यते नमःशब्देन सकारान्तेन नाम्‍ना तस्याविधानात्
children.translated_text: And this [dative] is not appropriate with the word <s>namaḥ</s> (salutation), because the use of that noun ending in the letter 'sa' is not prescribed [here].

children.text: न च प्रणम्येत्यत्र ल्यबन्ते सोस्ति । ल्यबन्तस्यैकदेशस्याप्रतिपादकत्वादसकारान्त
children.translated_text: Nor is it present in <s>praṇamya</s> (having bowed), which is an <s>lyap</s>-ending (absolutive) form, because the absolutive does not express a partial [action] and because it does not end in 'sa.'
Now, since [the person bowed to] is the object affected by the action of bowing, there should be the accusative case here; why then the dative?
'The action too must be understood' —

children.text: ति का त्या य न वचनात्पत्ये शेते
children.translated_text: according to the statement of <s>Kātyāyana</s>, the dative is used here as in '<s>patye śete</s>' (she lies down for the husband)

children.text: इत्यादिवदत्र चतुर्थी । भा ष्य कृ ता त्वयं सूत्रार्थ एवं वर्णितः । प्रार्थनाध्यवसाया
children.translated_text: and so forth. The <s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s> (author of the Bhāṣya), however, has explained this meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> thus: Through the desire constituting a purposive resolve and the like,
because [the recipient] is most desired to be attained through the action, having obtained the designation of object through the action of prostration by which [the recipient] is intended —

children.text: संप्रदानत्वविवक्षायामत्र चतुर्थी । यदा तु क्रियामात्रं क्रियान्तराव्याप्‍त्या विवक्ष्यते
children.translated_text: when one wishes to express the <s>sampradāna</s> (recipient) relation, the dative is used here. But when merely the action, without being pervaded by another action, is intended,
then the accusative is used for the object. And relying on this principle,
'[verbs of] motion and [their] objects' —
and so forth — the <s>sūtra</s> is to be understood

children.text: ख्यातम् । अमुना न्यायेनैव द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्योः सिद्धत्वात् न चातिप्रसंगः शिष्‍ट
children.translated_text: is well-known. Since the second and fourth cases are established by this very reasoning, there is no over-extension. [Following] the learned
usage, since [grammatical correctness] relies on worldly communicative intention, in other cases too, correctness is [determined] by the restriction of communicative intention alone.
This is observed. For instance, in forms like 'bruma' ('we speak'), the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) [is used]; otherwise,
when the result of the action is intended for the agent,

children.text: इत्यात्मनेपदमत्र स्यात् । वक्‍ता हि परं बोधयितुं वचनमुच्‍चारयन् क्रियाफल
children.translated_text: the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) would apply here. For a speaker, uttering speech in order to inform another, [becomes] connected with the result of the action,

children.text: योगी भवतीति नियतात्रात्मनेपदप्राप्‍तिः । अनुच्‍चारणव्यवच्छेदेन तु यदोच्‍चारणं
children.translated_text: and thus there would necessarily be the application of <s>ātmanepada</s> here. But when, by exclusion of non-utterance, the utterance

children.text: विवक्ष्यते तदा न न ब्रूमोऽपि तु ब्रूम एवेत्येतावन्मात्रविवक्षायां परस्मैपदं संगत
children.translated_text: is [what is] intended to be expressed, then—not 'we do not speak' but simply 'we speak'—in such a limited communicative intention, the <s>parasmaipada</s> is appropriate

indeed, and there is no fault. Even according to the view of the <s>sūtra</s>-author, since the designation <s>sampradāna</s> (recipient) has a consistent meaning, here too, with body, speech, and mind,

children.text: प्रणामेन भगवन्तमात्मसात्कुर्वन् स्तोत्रकर्त्ता च भगवते आत्मानं निवेदयतीति
children.translated_text: the one who composes the hymn, making the <s>Bhagavān</s> his own through homage, also offers himself to the <s>Bhagavān</s>—thus
he 'gives.'

Since there exists the state of being pleased through the action of prostration, which is pervaded by the action [of giving], the fourth case in the <s>sampradāna</s> (recipient) sense is indeed justified.

children.text: चतुर्थीति मु नि त्र य मतेप्यविरुद्धं साधुत्वं । जगद्धितैषिणे इति जगद्धितं सा ह्य
children.translated_text: Thus, the correctness [of the fourth case] is not contradicted even according to the view of <s>Munitraya</s> (the Three Sages). 'For the one who desires the welfare of the world'—the welfare of the world, that is indeed
the ultimate giving and receiving of what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted. Having bowed down with body, speech, and mind to the one whose nature is to seek that,

children.text: प्रणामं कृत्वा स मु च्‍च यः करिष्यते इति सम्बन्धः। एतेन प्रणामतः पूजा विहिता
children.translated_text: having performed homage, the 'collection' (<s>samuccaya</s>) will be composed—such is the syntactic connection. By this, worship through homage is enjoined.

children.text: शास्‍त्रे इति तृन्तृचौ शंसिक्षदादिभ्यः संज्ञायां चानिटावित्यौणादिक इट् प्रति्‍षेधः ।
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>śāstre</s>': the <s>tṛn</s> and <s>tṛc</s> suffixes, from roots like 'śaṃs', 'śikṣ', 'da', etc., in the sense of a proper name, the augment <s>iṭ</s> is prohibited according to the <s>Auṇādika</s> rule.
Teaching (<s>śāsana</s>) is instruction in the means for the cessation of suffering. And here it is intended [in reference to] the causal state and the resultant state. 'To the <s>Sugata</s>'—
Since it denotes the resultant state, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, performing that teaching, is not referred to by the word 'teacher' (<s>śāstṛ</s>) in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage,

children.text: नोक्‍तो मध्ये तु नमस्कारेणोभयावस्थायाः प्रणम्य तामाह । उभयी चावस्था हेतु
children.translated_text: but in the middle, through the salutation, having bowed to both states, he states that. And both states are of the nature of cause
and result. The causal state has the form of intention (<s>āśaya</s>) and practice (<s>prayoga</s>).
The intention, too, is twofold: having the aspect of protecting all beings, and having <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)

children.text: लम्बनः । प्रयोगोपि द्विधा विमुक्‍तिचर्याभावी भूमिगतश्‍च अधिमुक्‍तौ च प्रायोगि
children.translated_text: as its object. Practice, too, is twofold: that which is in the conduct leading to liberation, and that which belongs to the <s>bhūmi</s>s (stages). In the stage of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), the preliminary

children.text: को दानादयः । भूमौ तु वैपाकिकाः पारमिताख्याः
children.translated_text: practices are generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest. But on the <s>bhūmi</s>s (stages), they are the matured ones, called <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections).
These too are twofold: with volitional conditioning (<s>sābhisaṃskāra</s>) and

children.text: भिसंस्कारभेदेन । भूमयो हि सप्‍त साभिसंस्काराः । आभोगनिमित्तबलेन समाधेः
children.translated_text: without volitional conditioning (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>). For seven <s>bhūmi</s>s have volitional conditioning, since <s>samādhi</s> operates through the force of deliberate effort (<s>ābhoga</s>) and its cause (<s>nimitta</s>).

children.text: प्रवर्तनात्तत्रापि सप्‍तम्यां निमित्तं निवर्त्तते नाभोगं निमित्तशङ्कासद्भावादष्‍टम्यान्त्वा
children.translated_text: Even there, on the seventh [<s>bhūmi</s>], the cause ceases but not the deliberate effort, due to the presence of the apprehension of a cause. On the eighth, however,

children.text: भोगोपि निवर्तते शुद्धिभूमिप्राप्‍त्योभयनिवृत्तेः स्वरसवाही समाधिर्भवति । यद्वला
children.translated_text: the deliberate effort also ceases; through attaining the pure stages, with the cessation of both, <s>samādhi</s> becomes spontaneously flowing (<s>svarasavāhī</s>). By the power of which

is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). The causal state, being distinguished from the very beginning by four excellences, is superior to all [other paths].
It is said:
reverence—these are the four excellences. In this very lifetime, through practice in poetry, <s>śāstra</s>s (sciences), arts, and so forth, an unsurpassable
excellence of qualities arises.
Even that [excellence] by others is impossible to conceive. Likewise, through merit acquired in a single lifetime,
there comes about an unsurpassable excellence of the eight-fold lordship and other qualities among gods and others.
How much more, then, [for one who has attained] mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>),
who has attained it, whose accumulations of merit and knowledge are being augmented through unfailing practice over countless aeons—would he not reach the supreme

children.text: सम्पदमित्य(स)म्भाव्यमेतत् । कारणविशेषाच्‍च कार्य विशिष्यत इति फल

excellence is also distinguished in four ways, through the conjunction of the four excellences of abandonment, knowledge, form-body, and spiritual power. The excellence of abandon-

children.translated_text: ment is also described in four ways: the abandonment of all [afflictions], the complete abandonment, the abandonment of obstructions to all <s>samādhi</s>s and

children.translated_text: attainments. The excellence of knowledge is also distinguished in four ways: knowledge of all things, untaught

children.text: ज्ञानं अयुग्मज्ञानञ्‍च । रूपकायसंपदपि चतुर्विधा लक्षणसंपत् द्वात्रिंशन्महापुरुष
children.translated_text: knowledge, and unmatched knowledge. The excellence of the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) is also fourfold: excellence of the marks—through obtaining the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>);
excellence of the secondary characteristics—
through obtaining the eighty secondary characteristics; excellence of
strength—through being endowed with the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; and excellence of a diamond-essence bone-body—due to having a firm, indestructible body.
The excellence of spiritual power
is also
fourfold: the excellence of mastery over
creation, transformation, and governance of external objects;
the excellence of mastery over the governance and relinquishing of lifespan; the excellence of mastery over traveling to far-flung and obstructed spaces, entering few into many
and [many into few]; and the excellence of all <s>dharma</s>s with various innate wonders. The excellence of benefiting [others], too, belonging to both
states [causal and resultant], is distinguished in four ways: through turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>; through [liberating from] the three lower realms and <s>saṃsāra</s>
—by the nature of complete liberation from suffering; or by establishing [beings] in the happy destinations through the three vehicles.
Practice of the complete accumulations of merit and knowledge, uninterrupted practice, long-duration practice, and practice done with

children.translated_text: Or, '<s>Sugata</s>' means one who has gone to the beautiful, who has understood—thus [he is called] <s>Sugata</s>.
Here 'going' has the meaning of knowledge; but in the former [interpretation],

children.text: प्राप्‍तिवचनः । अनेन तु स्वार्थसम्पत्फलावस्थाभाविन्युक्‍ता । पूर्वन्तु हेतुभाविनी
children.translated_text: it means 'attainment.' By this [word <s>Sugata</s>], the resultant-state excellence for one's own sake is expressed. But the former [i.e., 'teacher'] expresses the causal-state

children.text: परार्थसम्पदुक्‍ता निरूपमां फलावस्थाभाविनीं परार्थंसम्पदमाह । तायिने इति ।
children.translated_text: excellence for the sake of others. He states the incomparable resultant-state excellence for the sake of others with '<s>tāyin</s>' (protector).

children.text: तायतेऽनेनेति तायः सुदृष्‍टमार्गोपदेशः । सोऽस्यास्तीति तायी । प्रेक्षावदारम्भाणां
children.translated_text: That by which one is protected is '<s>tāya</s>'—instruction in the well-discerned path. He who possesses that is '<s>tāyin</s>.' Since the undertakings of the discerning
are invariably accompanied by a purpose, he states the direct purpose: 'for the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition).' For the understanding of <s>pramāṇa</s>—

children.text: स्वप्रयोजनत्वान्‍नारब्धव्यमिदं प्रमाणसिद्धेर्न्या य मु खा दिनैव साधितत्वात्
children.translated_text: [Objection:] This [work] need not be undertaken, since it serves only its own purpose, and since the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s> has already been accomplished through the <s>Nyāyamukha</s> and other works.

children.text: यत् साधितं तत्र साध्यते यथा सिद्ध ओदनः इति
children.translated_text: [Reply:] What has been established there is [further] established [here], just as [one says] 'the rice is cooked' [even when it was already cooked].
Anticipating the objection of a pervading contradiction, [the commentator] says:
'Having departed from one's own doctrine'
—the ablative is in the sense of cause.
For the meaning of an expanded treatise is ascertained with difficulty;

children.text: इति सुखबोधायेहैकत्र व्यवस्थापितोऽशेषविमत्यपाकरणेनेति न पुनरुक्‍तता दोषः ।
children.translated_text: therefore, it has been consolidated here in one place for easy comprehension, with the removal of all doubts—thus there is no fault of repetition.

children.text: एकत इति सप्‍तम्यर्थे तसि (ः) । श्‍लोकश्‍चायं प्रमाणकथनप्रस्तावाद् भगवत्प्रामाण्य
children.translated_text: 'Ekataḥ'—the suffix '-tas' is in the sense of the locative. And this verse, in the context of discussing <s>pramāṇa</s>, establishes the authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
and should be understood both in forward (<s>anuloma</s>) and reverse (<s>pratiloma</s>) order.
'<s>Sugata</s>' means one who has well gone, who has attained—the complete abandonment of all that is to be abandoned, and the excellence of knowledge, etc.

children.text: प्रमाणं भगवान् जगद्धितैषित्वात् । यतश्‍च जगद्धितैषी अतः शास्ता

children.translated_text: And because

children.text: शासकोतो गोत्रभेदेन प्राज्ञजातीयत्वात् सुगतः। सुगतत्वाच्‍च सर्वजगत्त्रायकोऽतोयं
children.translated_text: he is a teacher, by the differentiation of lineage, being of the wise kind, he is <s>Sugata</s>. And because of being <s>Sugata</s>, he is the protector of all the world—therefore he
is a <s>pramāṇa</s>—this is the forward (<s>anuloma</s>) interpretation.
The <s>Bhagavān</s> is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority) because of desiring the welfare of the world. And because he desires the welfare of the world, therefore he is a teacher.

children.text: प्रतिलोमतस्तु प्रमाणं तायित्वात् । तायित्वं सुगतत्वात् । तच्‍च शास्तृत्वात् ।
एतच्‍च जगद्धितैषित्वात् । कार्यतः कारणानुमानमिति व्याख्याभेदः । तदत्र श्‍लोके
children.translated_text: And this is because of desiring the welfare of the world. [This is] inference from effect to cause—such is the alternative interpretation. Now in this verse,

children.text: शास्‍त्रकृता प्रथमार्द्धे पञ्‍च पदानि प्रणम्येत्येतत्त्यक्‍त्‏वाऽमुना परिच्छेदेन व्याख्यायन्ते ।
children.translated_text: the five words in the first half, excluding '<s>praṇamya</s>' ('having bowed'), are explained by the author of the <s>śāstra</s> in this section.
Not more [need be said], since it is easily understood—
In reverse (<s>pratiloma</s>), however: he is a <s>pramāṇa</s> because of being a protector (<s>tāyin</s>). Being a protector is due to being <s>Sugata</s>. And that is due to being a teacher.

children.text: देवतानां । भगवतस्त्वप्रतिसममहद्‍भूतगुणा स्तुतिरिति प्रतिहता अप्‍यत्र प्रवर्त्तन्ते ।
children.translated_text: deities consists of superimposed qualities. But the praise of the <s>Bhagavān</s> consists of incomparably great and real qualities—thus even the hostile are moved [by it].

children.text: मध्यस्था अभिप्रसीदन्ति । अभिप्रसन्‍नास्त्वत्यन्तमेव तत्र वृंहितभक्‍तयो भवन्ति । इति
children.translated_text: The neutral become favorably disposed. And those already favorably disposed become even more intensely devoted. Thus,

children.text: स्तोत्रकर्त्तुः परेषाञ्‍च पुण्योपचयो भवति । व्याख्यातुरपि तथैव सर्वं सम्पद्यते
children.translated_text: for the composer of the hymn and for others, there is an accumulation of merit. For the commentator too, everything is accomplished in the same way.
As it has been said:
since [only] what is worthy of explanation has been explained, the explanation of the verse is [complete], so he says. And generally, the praise of other
Just as the merit of the hymn-composer arises in the world through the praise,
so too does all [that merit] for the commentator—thus the commentary proceeds.
'<s>Pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is non-deceptive knowledge'—
and so forth. And this commentary is in the form of a <s>vārttika</s>

children.text: रूपेण चेयं व्याख्या । तल्लक्षणत्वादित्यर्थाक्षिप्‍तं । वार्त्तिकस्य च लक्षणमुक्‍तं ।
children.translated_text: (critical gloss). 'Because it has that definition'—this is implied by the meaning. And the definition of a <s>vārttika</s> has been stated.

children.text: वक्ष्यते व्याख्या चोद्देशनिर्देशापेक्षाक्षेपातिदेशादिलक्षणा तत्र युक्‍तात्र योज्या ।
children.translated_text: It will be said: 'Commentary has the characteristics of <s>uddeśa</s> (statement), <s>nirdeśa</s> (detailed exposition), <s>apekṣā</s> (reference), <s>ākṣepa</s> (implied meaning), <s>atideśa</s> (extension), etc.'—what is appropriate there should be applied here.

children.text: तत्रोद्देशनिर्देशौ समासव्यासकथनं । अपेक्षा च पूर्वोत्तराभ्यामपेक्षणं । आक्षेपोऽर्था
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>uddeśa</s> and <s>nirdeśa</s> are summary and detailed exposition. <s>Apekṣā</s> is reference to what precedes and follows. <s>Ākṣepa</s> is the stating of
implied meaning,
and exclusion from what is of a different kind.
And the author of the <s>śāstra</s> states that [definition]:

children.text: तदत्र वृ त्ति का रः श्‍लोकपातनिकां कुर्वन्

children.translated_text: 'for the one who has become a <s>pramāṇa</s>'—
explains this himself.

children.text: प्रमाणं जात इति भूतशब्दः प्रादुर्भावार्थः । तेनाजातमवस्थत्वान्‍न प्रमाणमित्य
children.translated_text: The word '<s>bhūta</s>' in 'one who has become (<s>jāta</s>) a <s>pramāṇa</s>' has the meaning of 'having come into being.' Therefore, [in a state of] not having arisen, one is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>—

children.text: नन्तरमुक्‍तम्वक्ष्यते च । सर्वश्‍च शब्दोऽन्यत्र प्रयुज्यमानोऽन्तर्भूतोपमार्थः प्रयुज्यत
children.translated_text: this has been stated afterward and will be stated [again]. And the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), when used elsewhere, is used with the included sense of comparison—
thus he says 'like a <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

children.text: प्रमाणशब्दो ज्ञाने मुख्य इतरत्र तु केन साधर्म्येणोपमानो
children.translated_text: The word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' is primary in [reference to] knowledge; but in other [applications], by what similarity does the comparison
constitute measurability? He says:
'Non-deceptive' (<s>avisaṃvādin</s>). But the verb 'bhavati' here means 'attainment'—
the meaning is clear,
therefore this

children.text: न विवृतः प्रामाण्यं प्राप्‍तः प्रमाणभूत इति ।
children.translated_text: is not elaborated [further]: 'having attained authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>), he has become a <s>pramāṇa</s>.'
Now here, the commentator (<s>vṛttikāra</s>), providing the lemma of the verse,
the nature of perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s> belongs [to him] directly—why resort to metaphor? If [one objects] thus, this fault [is answered]: with reference to the state of conceptual knowledge,
the statement is made—so say some. But what is appropriate here is this:
Although the <s>Bhagavān</s> is essentially a <s>pramāṇa</s> as described,
always, nonetheless that state-distinction is non-conventional; therefore, he is compared through conventional <s>pramāṇa</s>
for the purpose of instructing the world.
The liberated ones conduct themselves by this [conventional means] alone, not by the supramundane, since those others are not capable of perceiving
it. As it has been said:
Objection: Since [cognitions] produced by the power of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) are non-conceptual—[and yet] since the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s [knowledge] consists of conceptual and erroneous cognition,
In the worldly path, through designation and conventional expression,
knowledge and verbal expression are similar for both the ignorant and the wise.
'<s>Pramāṇa</s> is non-deceptive knowledge'—
Having restated non-deceptiveness and the nature of being knowledge, the authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>)
is prescribed. And this is the general definition pervading both types of <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: यद्यपि चालम्बनमनुमानस्य भ्रान्तं प्रवृत्तिविषयस्तु वाध एवार्थः । सामान्य
children.translated_text: Although the objective support (<s>ālambana</s>) of inference is erroneous, the object of its operation is indeed a real entity. Through the aspects of the universal and

the particular, since it determines the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone, non-deceptiveness is equal [for both perception and inference]. With respect to a [cognition's] connection with a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that is linked to
that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>), inference's operation is indeed toward the external [object]—thus the equality.

children.text: दोपि । तदाभासाभ्यामपि काकतालीयन्यायेन सम्वादोपि । अतः कथमेतत्प्रमाण
children.translated_text: can also occur. And even with their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), by the logic of the crow and the palm fruit [i.e., coincidence], non-deception can also occur. Therefore, how is this a definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>?
Objection: Even for one who acts based on perception and inference, since obstruction and such are sometimes possible, deception

children.text: न दोषः । सदैव प्रमाणाभ्यां प्रवृत्तस्य प्रतिबन्धादप्रतिबन्धादिसम्भवे नियतः
सम्वादो न त्वेवं तदाभासेऽवश्‍यम्भावी सम्वादः । प्रमाणशक्‍तिर्वा प्रामाण्यं सा च
children.translated_text: non-deception; but it is not the case that with their semblances non-deception necessarily occurs. Or, authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is the capacity of <s>pramāṇa</s>, and that

children.text: प्रतिबन्धादावप्यस्ति प्रमाणयोर्न त्वेवं तदाभासयोरिति असाङ्कर्यमेव । द्विविधश्‍च
children.translated_text: exists in the two <s>pramāṇa</s>s even when there is obstruction, but not so in their semblances—thus there is no confusion at all. And non-deception is twofold:

children.text: सम्वादो ज्ञेयधर्मो ज्ञानधर्मश्‍च । अत्रार्थमुपलभ्य प्रवृत्ताविष्‍टार्थप्राप्‍तिः सम्वादो
children.translated_text: a property of the object-to-be-known, and a property of knowledge. Here, the attainment of the desired object after perceiving the object and acting [upon it] is non-deception as

a property of the object, since it is established through the capacity of the object. But the comprehension of causal efficacy through the arising of knowledge bearing its form is a property of the subject (<s>viṣayin</s>),

children.text: सत्यपि बाह्येऽर्थे तद्व‍्यवस्थाश्रयं ज्ञानमेव तस्य स्वसम्विद्रूपतया
children.translated_text: Even though the external object exists, the basis for its determination is knowledge alone, because of its nature as self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>);
it illuminates the external [object] because it is self-luminous in nature.
Thus, since non-deception as a property of the object is also possible,
the inclusion of the word 'knowledge' [in the definition] has been made—explaining this, he says:
'That [non-deception], when the object is to be determined—'
and so forth. 'That non-deception again'

children.text: विषयधर्म इत्यनेन सम्बन्धः । कदा पुनरसौ भवतीत्याह । अर्थस्य विच्छिद्य
children.translated_text: —the connection is with 'as a property of the object.' When does it occur? He says: 'Having determined the object'

children.text: प्रवृत्ताविति । परिच्छेदः प्रमाणद्वयं । तत्तु इत्यत्रानयोः । प्रत्यासन्‍नकारणत्वमिति
children.translated_text: and then acting—'determination' means the two <s>pramāṇa</s>s. 'That, however'—here, of these two. [The word] indicates being the proximate cause.

children.text: सूचयति । अयन्तु भेदः प्रत्यक्षाविकल्पकत्वान्‍न निश्‍चयः किन्तु तदाभासोत्पत्तेः ।
children.translated_text: But this is the distinction: perception, being non-conceptual, does not [produce] a determination, but [acts] through the arising of its semblance.

children.text: अनुमाने तु निश्‍चय एव । यद्येवं प्रत्यक्षेणाविकल्पेन मिथ्याफलवादिनां विवेकस्य
children.translated_text: In inference, however, there is determination proper. If so, since for those who hold that the result [of perception] is erroneous, discrimination through non-conceptual perception
is impossible to achieve—how can there be action after determining the object from that [perception]? If [one objects] thus—
It is replied:
Action based on perception is twofold:

children.text: प्रत्यक्षाश्रया प्रवृत्तिराद्याभ्यासवती च । तत्र याऽद्या सार्थगता तत्राभ्याससामर्थ्याद्यथा
children.translated_text: initial and habituated through practice. Of these, the first, which is accompanied by the object—in that case, through the power of practice, just as
knowledge of genuine and counterfeit gems, silver, and such, arising with acquired expertise regarding the subject matter, determines the form exactly as the thing is,
so it arises [determining correctly]. And the awareness of that form is the comprehension of the external object, since the existence of the object is established in consciousness.
And awareness, having a definite form, is the determiner of objects through their twofold nature.
And by virtue of this, the conceptual construction of positive and negative

children.text: विकल्पः । इदमुपलभे इदं नोपलभ इति भवति । तथा भूतं तत्स्वत एव प्रमाणं पुरुषं
children.translated_text: [arises]: 'This I perceive; this I do not perceive.' Such being the case, that [perception], being by its own nature a <s>pramāṇa</s>, impels a person

children.text: बाह्येऽर्थे प्रवर्त्तयतीत्यर्थं परिच्छिद्येति वचनं घटत एव

But for one whose discrimination is not determined,

children.text: कारणपरिशुद्धिद्वारेण प्रवृत्ति (ः।) अत्रापि योऽसमर्थस्तस्य संशयेनैव प्रवृत्तिः ।

children.text: तत्राद्येन हेतुद्वयेन यः प्रवर्त्तते निवर्त्तते च पश्‍चाद् येन स प्रेक्षापूर्वकारी भण्यते

For indeed,

And the logical reason is not indicative merely by [its] being seen or not seen, but rather
by [its] necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>).

children.text: स च द्विरूपो नार्थलक्षणो विरोधस्य [परस्य न परिहारस्त्विति

Likewise, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other)

children.text: न च विधिमुखेन शब्दे वाचकः किन्त्वन्यव्य
children.translated_text: Nor is [a word] a signifier of [its referent] through positive affirmation, but through the exclusion of others—

by exclusion of absence [because it signifies by excluding existence], just as in existence too, by the force of exclusion of others [as in exclusion-inclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) such as 'non-Brahmins' etc.],

children.text: पर्युदासे]च्छेदबलादेव च विशिष्‍टार्थप्रतीतेरन्यथा यत एव विजातीयान्‍न निवर्तेतं
children.translated_text: the cognition of a qualified meaning [arises]; otherwise, since [the word] would not exclude what is heterogeneous,
it could also be of another form.
It would be another, either possessing that form or possessing its own form, due to non-exclusion. And word is not authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>),
because it is an effect of [the speaker's] intention to express—all this was stated in the first chapter.
Thus,
Inference is twofold: for one's own sake (<s>svārtha</s>), apprehending the object through the logical mark having three characteristics.
As before, the result is the object and [its] own form—these two are not equal.

children.text: अत्र प्र मा ण स मु च्‍च ये द्वितीयपरिच्छेदश्‍लोके पूर्ववदिति प्रत्यक्ष इव विषया

children.translated_text: is not different from the means of valid cognition; this should be understood also in inference. The object, however, is: for perception, the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>);

children.text: स्वलक्षणमितरस्य तु सामान्याकारोन्यापोहो विषयः स्वरूपञ्‍च स्पष्‍टास्पष्‍टप्रतिभा
children.translated_text: for the other [i.e., inference], the universal form, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other), is the object. And the own form—the clear and unclear appearance—
is equally the same for perception and inference. This, setting aside the inference to be discussed later as a topic of great debate...
Here, in the verse of the second chapter of the <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s>, 'as before' [means that] just as in perception, the result—which is of the nature of apprehension of the object—

children.text: अधुना शेष प्र मा ण स मु च्‍च य प्रथमद्वितीयपरिच्छेदव्याचिख्या
children.translated_text: Now, having explained the remaining <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s>, the first and second chapters,

children.text: सुस्तदादिनमस्कारश्‍लोकं च व्याख्यातुं शास्‍त्रकारो द्वितीयपरिच्छेदं प्रस्तौति ।
children.translated_text: in order to explain the opening salutation verse, the author of the treatise introduces the second chapter.
And next, in the investigation of scripture (<s>āgama</s>)—
having refuted human-authored scripture, what was promised—that the indicator of all

children.text: दृष्‍टादृष्‍टप्रकर्षार्थस्य स्वर्गापवर्गादेः परलोकस्य च देशकः पुरुषातिशय एवेति स

children.text: इदानीं प्रमाणभूतः साध्यते नेश्‍वरादिरिति कथ्यते प्रवचने चार्यसत्यचतुष्‍टयं दुःख
children.translated_text: he [such a person] is now established as authoritative, not God (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like—thus it is stated. And in the teaching, the noble Four Truths (<s>āryasatyacatuṣṭaya</s>), the truth of suffering
being primary, were stated in the order of examination.
For the <s>yogin</s>, afflicted by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), first examining the truth of suffering,

children.text: निरूप्य हेयोपादेयं सोपायं पर्येषत इति कृत्वा शास्‍त्रकारस्तूत्पत्तिक्रममाश्रित्य यथा
children.translated_text: seeks what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted, together with the means. Therefore, the author of the treatise, relying on the order of origination—how

children.text: संसारः प्रवर्त्तते निवर्तते च तथा प्रथमं समुदयसत्यं तद्विमतिनिराकरणतः
children.translated_text: <s>saṃsāra</s> operates and how it ceases—first states the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>), refuting disputes about it,
and then in sequence states the remaining three truths, refuting all disputes—this is the meaning of the second chapter.

children.text: च्छेदार्थः । सर्वत्र च प्रेक्षावतां सम्बन्धं विना वाञ्छाप्रवृत्तिरिति पूर्वापरपरि
children.translated_text: And everywhere, since for the discerning, desire and action do not arise without [understanding] the connection, the connection must necessarily be stated for joining the earlier and later chapters.

And that [connection] is characterized by immediate succession; even for successive [chapters], because benefit exists from the earlier ones. And immediate succession is of two kinds: textual and semantic.
Since treatises and the like are of the nature of word and meaning, therein the connection of the immediately following chapter—'this is the second chapter.'
For those unable to comprehend reality, through good conduct, the determination of means of valid cognition and objects of knowledge—
this exposition following the teaching of the Master is stated.

children.text: ये पुद्‍गलाः परमार्थाधिगमे झटित्यसक्‍ता धर्मानुसारिणो योगिनश्‍च तेषां

children.translated_text: through correct conventional [practice], the determination of means of valid cognition and objects of knowledge [is made], since [such determination] is impossible in the ultimate [sense]. As the crest-jewel of the <s>Naiyāyika</s> circle stated in the <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s>:

thus. For the other [person] is indeed the one to be made to understand

For this is not a royal decree that the thesis must be proven

children.text: नैव साध्यं साधनीयमिति । पञ्‍चविंशतितत्त्वसंख्यानकुशलाः सां ख्या ऊचुः
children.translated_text: only with what is established for both parties. The <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, skilled in the enumeration of twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (categories of reality), said to the Buddhists:

children.translated_text: 'Pleasure and the like are unconscious, or the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) [is unconscious], because [they are] produced, or because [they are] eternal, like form and the like.' [This was argued against the Buddhists.]

children.text: बौद्धेन ह्यान्तराश्‍चिद्रूपाश्‍च सुखादयो बुद्धिश्‍चेष्‍टाः । असद्वादी च बौद्धोऽसदेवोत्प
children.translated_text: For the Buddhist accepts that pleasure and the like are internal and of the nature of consciousness, as is the intellect. And the Buddhist, being an <s>asadvādin</s> (proponent of non-pre-existence of the effect), [holds that] what is non-existent indeed arises, because effects arise from the force of causes.

children.text: न हि कार्यं स्वतन्त्रमुत्पद्यते निरन्वयञ्‍च नाशमि
children.translated_text: For an effect does not arise independently, nor does it perish without a trace. But the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, being a <s>sadvādin</s> (proponent of the pre-existence of the effect), [holds that] for him, only what [already] exists arises as an effect, existing even in the prior state in the form of a seed.

children.text: च्छति । सांख्यस्तु सद्वादी तस्य सदेव कार्यमुत्पद्यते बीजभावेन प्रागवस्थायामपि

with a beloved.

Absence (<s>abhāva</s>)

children.text: अभावः । नैवाभावः कश्‍चित्सर्वेषां कथञ्‍चिद् भावादिति चेत् ।
children.translated_text: Absence. 'There is no absence at all, since everything exists in some way'—if so,

children.text: यथा तेन सन्तं सप्रकारोऽभावः । शशविषाणयोश्‍चायं भावात् शशविषाणाभाव
children.translated_text: then by that very [argument], existence has a specific form of absence. And this—[the claim that] since the hare and horns exist, [there is no] absence of hare's horns—
one who ridicules the proponent of the absence of hare's horns ridicules himself. The import of [the opponent's] attack is that the horn, which would be a part of the hare, does not exist.

children.text: प्रस्तावः । शशोप्‍यस्ति विषाणञ्‍चेत्युत्तरस्य । न ह्ययं विषाणमात्रमपह्नुते ।
children.translated_text: The response is: the hare exists and the horn also [exists separately]. For he does not deny the horn as such,

children.text: यतस्तेन प्रतिरुद्ध‍्येत किन्तु शशसम्बन्धि । यद्येवं सम्बन्धो नास्तीति वक्‍तव्यं न
children.translated_text: since he would be contradicted by that. Rather, [he denies] what is connected with the hare. If so, one should say 'the connection does not exist,' not 'the horn.'

children.text: विषाणम् । किम्वै सम्बन्धमात्रं विशिष्‍यते । विषाणिनामपि विषाणेषु द्रव्यस्वभावः ।
children.translated_text: What indeed is distinguished by the connection alone? For even among horned [animals], the horns have the nature of substance.
And the nature too varies for each effect, due to the difference of causes.
Therefore, the reproach is: what is this absence of connection that is to be stated?

children.text: अस्ति विषाणिनां विषाणस्वभावभेदो न तद्वत् किञ्‍चित् शशस्य भिन्‍न
children.translated_text: There is a difference in the nature of horns among horned [animals]; no such distinct

children.translated_text: nature of horns exists for the hare—if so. We too say exactly this. Or, what is desired as 'the connection does not exist'—that itself is the absence.

children.text: ष्यते स एवाभावः । सम्बन्धी विद्यते न सम्बन्ध इति चेत् निपुणा वाचो युक्‍तिः ।

children.text: अङ्गीकृतसम्बन्धं द्रव्यमपि नेति चेत् । प्रियमनुष्‍ठितं यदीदमेव प्रथममभिधीयते
children.translated_text: Even the substance with an accepted connection—'does not exist'—if so, [that is] a welcome performance. If this very thing is stated first,

children.translated_text: the opponent would not be troubled—thus. The contradictory non-deviating [reason] (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) is also stated as a reason for doubt;

Refutation of the doctrine of consciousness of material elements (<s>bhūtacaitanya</s>)
For the <s>āstikas</s> (affirmers), consciousness, distinct from the great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>), transmigrates even to another birth.

children.text: नास्तिकानान्तु महाभूताव्यतिरिक्‍तं दृष्‍टमात्रे ह्येवं ते प्राहुः । महाभूतानामेवाभि

children.text: व्यक्‍तिविशेषो मदशक्‍तिवच्‍चैतन्यमिति । अभिव्यक्‍तं चैतन्यं यस्मिन्देहे स तथाभूतो

children.text: देहः स्वभावो यस्य पुरुषस्य स तथा । पश्‍चाद् घटशब्देन द्वन्द्वः । निर्द्धारणे षष्‍ठ्‍याः

children.text: सप्‍तम्या वा द्विवचनमेतत् । अवयवावयविसम्बन्धे वा षष्‍ठी । तयोरन्यतरेण घटेन
children.translated_text: or by the person—it coexists with the second; and thus [it is called] 'the second.'

children.text: पुरुषेण वा सह द्वितीयेन वर्त्तत इति च द्वितीयः । व्याजेन च महाभूताव्यतिरिक्‍तं
children.translated_text: And by this stratagem, one attempts to prove through a syllogism that consciousness is distinct from the great elements.

children.text: चैतन्यं प्रयोगेण साधयति । अस्ति हि दृष्‍टान्तेऽनुत्पत्यात्मकस्य कुड्यस्यान्यतरेण
children.translated_text: For in the example, the wall—which is of the nature of non-origination—has coexistence with one or the other, namely the pot; even coexistence with just one—coexistence with one or the other is established in general—

children.text: घटेन सद्वितीयत्वमेकेनापि सद्वितीयत्वेऽन्यतरेण सद्वितीयत्वं सामान्येन सिद्धमिति
children.translated_text: thus the illustration is not tainted by the thesis.

children.text: न साध्येनान्वितं निदर्शनम् । तथा घटस्यापि साध्यधर्मिणोऽशेषघटपक्षीकरणे
children.translated_text: Likewise, even for the pot, which is the subject of the thesis—when all pots are included in the thesis,

children.text: तेनैव सद्वितीयत्वमयुक्‍तमिति सामान्येनापि साधने तथाभूतेन पुरुषेण सद्वितीयत्वं
children.translated_text: coexistence with that very [pot] would be improper; thus even in general proof, coexistence with such a person
is established by elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>)—so the mind thinks.
Here—
and so forth. Even without stating such a person,
because [such a person] is the thesis to be proven, being pervaded by desire, and because of its being unestablished—there is the fault of non-connection (<s>ananvaya</s>) in the example.

children.text: सामान्येनेति । तादृशैव पुंसा विशेषणेन सद्वितीयत्वं साध्यते घटस्य यतो विशेषा
children.translated_text: 'By [a property] common to the thesis'—with such a person as the qualifier, coexistence is to be proven for the pot; since with reference to the particular, there would be two faults; but

children.text: पेक्षया दोषद्वयं स्यात्किन्तु सामान्येनान्यतरसद्वितीयत्वं धर्मिणो वक्‍तुमिष्‍टमतो
children.translated_text: coexistence with one or the other in general is intended to be stated of the subject—therefore this [charge of] fault is without substance, because the general [property] itself does not exist.

children.text: यमदोष इत्यसारम् । सामान्यस्यैवाभावात् । सद्वितीयं हि घटेन वा स्यादुक्‍त
children.translated_text: For coexistence would be either with the pot or with the stated person. In the case of the pot, since it is taken as the subject of the thesis, coexistence with it [cannot be proven] due to identity—

children.text: पुरुषेण वा । तत्र घटस्य साध्यधर्मित्वेनाश्रयणाम् नानेन सद्वितीयत्वमभेदात्
children.translated_text: for coexistence requires a basis of difference. Nor with the person, due to the fault of non-connection—thus he says:

children.text: भेदाधिष्‍ठानं हि सद्वितीयत्वं । नापि पुरुषेणानन्वयदोषादिति । एतदेवाह

children.translated_text: 'general [property] is not established'—
That very
and so forth. By the non-authoritative [teachers], the admission is [that] in the stated manner, [an entity] internal to bodies is not
admitted by the opponent, due to faults such as non-connection.
'Equally, even in destruction'—

children.text: ति । यथा हि घटेन घटस्य सद्वितीयत्वं
children.translated_text: thus. Just as coexistence of the pot with the pot
is to be proven as the thesis due to contradiction; nor should non-connection be suspected with such a person—thus, in the absence of both, proof through the general [property]—so too here, he says.
'By the difference of the word pot'—
and so forth. In [the case of] sound, the impermanence of sound is not
the thesis, due to the suspicion of non-connection. Nor is the impermanence of the pot the thesis in [the case of] sound, due to impossibility. And if
the impermanence of the pot is predicated of sound, then there is contradiction with what is accepted,

children.text: घटानित्यत्वं शब्दं प्रति ज्ञायते तदाभ्युपेतविरोधः । शब्दे घटानित्यत्वस्यानभ्युप
children.translated_text: because the impermanence of the pot is not accepted [as applying] to sound. By the word 'etc.,' contradiction with inference also [is included], since another property's being sublated elsewhere [is possible].
And if [one] constructs [the argument] through the difference of [the word] 'sound,' there is the fault of the thesis being deficient in the example.

children.text: कल्पने साध्यविकलतादोषो दृष्‍टान्ते । असिद्धेन विनाशेनेति । धर्मिविशेषापरिग्रहेण
children.translated_text: 'With an unestablished destruction'—because, without specifying the particular subject, destruction in general is established.
'Of that which possesses [destruction]'—
thus, of that which possesses destruction.
but [the opponent], having conceived [the argument] differently, has produced [what he claims is] an equal fault—to state this, he says:
'For not'—
and so forth.

children.text: अन्यतरार्थान्तरत्वं सामान्यं घटे साध्यधर्मिणि कुड्‏ये च दृष्‍टान्तधर्मिणि उपनीत
children.translated_text: The otherness-of-one-or-the-other [quality], [which is] general, is applied in the pot—the subject of the thesis—and in the wall—the subject of the example—

children.text: मिति प्रतिक्षिप्‍तं साध्यमिष्‍टं परस्य साध्यधर्मिगतम्वान्यतरार्थान्तरत्वं साध्यं
children.translated_text: thus the refuted thesis is the one desired by the opponent, either as otherness-of-one-or-the-other belonging to the subject of the thesis

children.text: दृष्‍टान्तधर्मिगतम्वेति यावत् । कुतो नानात्वे सति नानत्वेति तत् (?) न ह्यत्रा
children.translated_text: or belonging to the subject of the example. Why, when there is diversity, is there diversity? That is [the question].

children.text: न्यतरार्थान्तरत्वं कुड्‏यधर्मो घटेस्ति साध्यं नापि घटधर्मः कुड्‏ये साध्यमिष्‍टमन्वे
children.translated_text: For here, the otherness-of-one-or-the-other, which is a property of the wall, does not exist in the pot as the thesis; nor is the property of the pot

children.text: तीति साध्यवैकल्यादिकं व्रूमो येन तुल्यदोषता स्यात् साध्यधर्म एव तादृश इति
children.translated_text: the intended thesis in the wall—thus we state the deficiency of the thesis and the like, whereby there would be an equal fault. The property to be proven is itself of such a nature.
Just as, with reference to the stated person and pot, the otherness-of-one-or-the-other, when examined, is not established.

children.text: न हि घटस्यार्थान्तरभावो विरोधात् । देहस्याप्यनन्वयाशङ्कया नेष्यते तेनेत्येतावता
children.translated_text: For the otherness of the pot [from itself] is contradictory. And [otherness] of the body is also not desired, due to the suspicion of non-connection—therefore, by this much,
in general, sound is proven [impermanent]—through the exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>); [the opponent] desires non-connection with some [form of] impermanence—thus
that connection is to be established.
'If there were otherness, that pot too would have it'—
in order to explain this <s>sūtra</s>, he says:
'But the otherness-of-one-or-the-other'—

children.text: ति । तु शब्दो विशेषे । यथाऽनित्यत्वं वस्तुधर्मो न
children.translated_text: thus. The word 'but' [indicates] a distinction. Just as impermanence is a property of [real] things,

children.text: तथा सद्वितीयत्वं वस्तुधर्मः । इच्छाबलेन च व्यवस्थापनात् । न ह्येतत्कार्यं
children.translated_text: coexistence is not likewise a property of [real] things—because it is established by the force of desire. For this is not the effect

children.text: स्वभावो वा भावस्य युज्यते त्विच्छाबलेन संचार्यार्थान्तरत्वेपि वर्त्तमानत्वात् ।
children.translated_text: or own-nature of an entity; but by the force of desire, since [the quality of] otherness is present even when [the entity is conceptually] relocated.
'That pot [would] have it'—the explanation of this is: a pot coexisting with one or the other...
We have stated the deficiency of agreement (<s>anvaya</s>) and the like when the coexistence-argument is formulated in another way;
The logical reason (<s>hetu</s>)

children.text: कान्तिक एव प्राणादिः । साधारणमपि खलु प्रमेयत्वमसंस्कृताप-
children.translated_text: Only the <s>Kāntika</s> [school holds that] <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the like [are the soul]. Even the common [property of] being an object of valid cognition [is disputed by] those who deny the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>).

children.text: वादिनः । असमन्वययोगात् । अव्यभिचारितान्वयः स पक्ष एवास्तीति ।
children.translated_text: Due to the impossibility of agreement (<s>samanvaya</s>). [The logical mark] having unfailing agreement exists only in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus).

children.text: अन्वयिनमेव हेतुमाह । अत्रापि कथमव्यतिरेको विपक्षात् । कथम्वा सपक्ष
एवास्तीति । किं (सप) क्षस्यावधारणस्य फलं यदि न विपक्षेऽस्तित्वं व्यवच्छिद्यते
children.translated_text: What is the purpose of the determination of the <s>sapakṣa</s> if it does not exclude existence in the <s>vipakṣa</s>?

children.text: व्यवच्छेदे वा कथमव्यतिरेकः । न हि सत्ता प्रतिषेधादन्यो व्यतिरेकः । विप्रतिषिद्धं
children.translated_text: And if it does exclude, how is there non-negative agreement (<s>avyatireka</s>)? For negative agreement (<s>vyatireka</s>) is nothing other than the negation of existence. And this is

children.text: चैतत् । नान्वयो न व्यतिरेक इति । य एव खलु नेत्यन्वयप्रतिषेधः स एव
children.translated_text: contradictory: 'neither [positive] agreement nor negative agreement.' For what is indeed the negation of [positive] agreement
is itself the negative agreement. Then this comes to [the position that] there is no negative agreement of the non-existent. Here, this alone is to be said again:

children.text: कथमसतोऽन्वयप्रतिषेध इति वस्तुरूपानुकर्षी खल्वसति प्रतिषेधो न सम्भवेत् । न हि
children.translated_text: 'How is there negation of agreement for the non-existent?'—for negation, which involves the engagement with the form of a [real] thing, cannot apply to what is non-existent. For not
<s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally-bound negation) alone is the domain of the negative particle. What then?
There is also the negation by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣapratiṣedha</s>). For there is no contradiction of that in what is non-existent.

children.text: विरोधः । सो पि न सम्भवति । अधिकरणाद्यर्थानां प्रतिषेधविषयोपदर्शिनीनां
children.translated_text: That too is not possible, because the case-endings and the like, which indicate the object of negation—

children.text: विभक्‍तीनामयोगादिति चेत् । उक्‍तोत्तरमेतत् । तस्मान्‍न हेतुः कश्‍चिदन्वयी
children.translated_text: If [one objects] that there is no connection of case-endings [in the example], this has already been answered. Therefore, there is no reason whatsoever that is purely positive (<s>anvayī</s>),

children.text: नाम । न च प्रमेयत्वस्य विपक्षेऽन्वयात्मा सः । त्रिविधो हि धर्मो भावाभावोभयाश्रय
children.translated_text: nor is that [reason] of the nature of positive concomitance with regard to <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) in the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>). For a property (<s>dharma</s>) has been stated to be of three kinds: based on existence, non-existence, or both.

children.text: इत्युक्‍तः । नाभावस्य कश्‍चिद्धर्म इति चेत् । नन्वयमेवास्य धर्मविरहो धर्मः ।
children.translated_text: If [one says] that non-existence has no property — well, this very absence of properties is its property.

children.text: न हि वस्तुरूपमेव धर्मा असन्तोपि हि केनचित्प्रकरणेन इमं व्यवहारमुपनीयन्ते ।
children.translated_text: For properties are not necessarily of the nature of real entities; even non-existent things are brought into this usage by some contextual reason.

children.text: अन्यथा हि तत्राव्यवहार एव स्यात् । न च सतामपि परमार्थतः कश्‍चिद्धर्मधर्मिभावः ।
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be no usage at all regarding those [non-existent things]. And even for existing things, there is ultimately no real property-property-bearer relationship.

children.text: केवलं बुद्धिरेव सम्बन्धमुपरचयतीत्युक्‍तं वा र्ति के । बुद्धिकृता च घटनाऽसत्सु केन
children.translated_text: It has been said in the <s>Vārttika</s> that the intellect alone constructs the relation. And what prevents the intellect from making connections even regarding non-existent things?
The categories of existent, non-existent, both, and neither, for those who hold different philosophical systems, have uncertain means of proof and do not yield
exclusive apprehension. Therefore, however they may be determined by this [analysis], those that are <s>prameya</s> (knowable)

children.text: वक्‍तव्याः । न हि भावविषयमेव प्रमाणं । अविसंवादलक्षणत्वात्‍प्रमाणस्य । उल्लसती
children.translated_text: should be stated. For valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) does not pertain only to existing things, since <s>pramāṇa</s> is defined by non-deceptiveness. Whatever arises

children.text: तद्वारे न व्यवस्थापयेत् । न चेत्स्वविषये परेण वाध्येत । तदन्यप्रमाणलक्षणम
children.translated_text: at that occasion it should establish — and should not be contradicted by another [cognition] regarding its own object. That is the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> for [establishing] the other [i.e., the knowable].
Thus the <s>prameya</s> (knowable)...........

He states that the logical reason is only that which has [positive] agreement (<s>anvaya</s>). Here too, how is there non-deviation from the dissimilar instances (<s>vipakṣa</s>)? And how does it exist only in the similar instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>)?
Non-deception with respect to intention —
etc.
The light of a gem and a lamp —
and so on —

children.text: त्यादि वा र्ति क श्‍लो क द्वयवृत्तौ वक्ष्यते ।
children.translated_text: etc., will be explained in the commentary on the two <s>Vārttika</s> verses.
If, regarding the light of a gem, the cognition of a gem — even though erroneous — is accepted as inference because of [its] concordance,
and is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) because of the statement of non-deceptiveness, then a third <s>pramāṇa</s> distinct from perception and inference
would be entailed.

children.text: तथा हि मणिप्रभायां मणिबुद्धेर्न प्रत्यक्षं भ्रान्तत्वात्सविकल्पकत्वाच्‍च ।
children.translated_text: For indeed, the gem-cognition in the light of a gem is not perception, because it is erroneous and because it is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>).

children.text: प्रत्यक्षत्वं त्वेतद्विपरीतं । नाप्‍यनुमानमलिङ्गजत्वात् । न चाप्रमाणं वस्तुसम्वादात् ।
children.translated_text: Perceptuality is the opposite of that. Nor is it inference, since it does not arise from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Nor is it a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, since it accords with reality.
Some say:
For the general definition of inference
will be established immediately hereafter:
Inference is the apprehension of something remote through its connection with something else.

children.text: इह च मणौ मणिप्रभासम्बन्धात्तत्कार्यत्वात् तस्याश्‍च प्रभायं मणिभ्रान्तिरुत्पद्यते
children.translated_text: And here, because of the connection of the gem-light with the gem — since [the light] is its effect — an erroneous cognition of a gem arises in that light.
Therefore, since it arises from an effect-mark (<s>kāryaliṅga</s>), it is indeed inference. As follows:
In the gem-light, at first, a non-erroneous

children.text: मेव चक्षुर्विज्ञानमुपजायते । तेन च कार्यलिङ्गस्वरूपमधिगतं यतः स्वलक्षण
children.translated_text: visual cognition arises. Through that, the essential nature of the effect-mark is apprehended, since the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone is the logical mark. And the capacity to indicate is established through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). And of a superimposed form,

children.text: मेव लिङ्गं । तादात्म्यतदुत्पत्तिभ्यां च गमकत्वं स्थितं । न च कल्पितरूपस्या
children.translated_text: there is no otherness, nor are there identity and causal origination [with the superimposed].
To this we reply: this is indeed inference.

children.text: कथं स्वलक्षणेनान्वय इति चेत् । न ब्रूमस्तेनैवेति किन्तु तज्‍जातीयेन स्वल

children.translated_text: "Even one of the same class, when non-difference is intended, is that very [thing]."
Therefore, particulars of the same class (<s>samānajātīya-svalakṣaṇa</s>), qualified by exclusion from dissimilar things (<s>vijātīya-vyāvṛtti</s>), when considered in their totality,

children.text: पेक्षितानि सामान्यमित्युच्यन्ते । यत्रापि कृतकत्वादयो व्यवस्थाप्‍यन्ते तत्रापि मूढ
children.translated_text: are called the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>). And even where properties like being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) are established, there too the division into property and property-bearer
is a device for instructing the confused.
The logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that indicates is indeed the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone.
And thus [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:

"The distinction into property and property-bearer is conceptually constructed, not real." When a cognition arises in the property-bearer (<s>liṅgin</s>) from the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) such as smoke, it does not operate through superimposition on the smoke alone, but on another location. But the gem-

children.text: नि ज्ञानमुत्पद्यमानं न धूम एवाध्यारोपेण प्रवर्त्तते किन्त्वन्यत्र प्रदेशे । मणि
children.translated_text: error superimposes the property-bearer (<s>liṅgin</s>) upon the very mark (<s>liṅga</s>) called gem-light — if [one objects thus], then what of it?

children.text: भ्रान्तिस्तु मणिप्रभाख्य एव लिङ्गे लिङ्गिनमारोपयन्तीति चेत् । ततः किं न (:)
children.translated_text: Let that not be diminished.
What is diminished is [only] the fact of being produced from a connection — there is additionally a spatial error here, that much we say.
In that very

children.text: देशे मणिप्राणकत्वे माभूत्प्रामाण्यं मणिमात्रप्रापणे तु केनानुमानत्वं वार्यते
children.translated_text: location, let there not be validity regarding the gem's being alive, but who can prevent its being inference with respect to [indicating] a gem in general?
All inference is accepted as erroneous. If [one says] there is no recollection of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) in the gem-error —

children.text: चेत् । यदि नास्ति न तावतानुमानत्वाभावः यो ह्यन्वयव्यतिरेकावस्मृत्वा द्रागेव
children.translated_text: even if there is none, that alone does not negate its being inference. For one who, without remembering positive and negative concomitance, quickly cognizes fire from smoke — is that cognition then not accepted as inference?

children.text: धूमाद्वह्निं प्रत्येति तदा किं तज्ज्ञानमनुमानं नेष्‍यते । त्रिरूपात्तु लिङ्गात्तदुत्पद्यत
children.translated_text: We say it is inference simply because it arises from a logical mark possessing the three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>). If the gem-error in the gem-light is indeed inference, then for what purpose

children.text: इत्येतावतानुमानमिति ब्रुमः । यद्यनुमानमेव मणिप्रभायां मणिभ्रान्तिः किमर्थं
children.translated_text: is it used as an illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>)?

It is not proper for inference itself to serve as an illustration when non-deceptiveness in general is what is being proved for inference. This too is not a fault, because even though there is erroneousness in the gem-error, the opponent desires only the speaker's

children.text: स्यैव दृष्‍टान्तत्वं युक्‍तं । अयमप्‍यदोषो यतो मणिभ्रान्ते भ्रान्तत्वेपि परो वक्‍तृविस
children.translated_text: non-deception. But for other logical marks such as smoke, non-erroneousness means appearing as a real object —

children.text: म्वादमात्रमिच्छति । अन्यस्य तु धूमादिलिङ्गस्याभ्रान्तत्वं वस्तुप्रतिभासित्वं चान्यथा
children.translated_text: otherwise there would be no non-deceptiveness — and therefore the gem-error is employed as an illustration.

children.text: तदेतद्वहुतरञ्‍च दुःखञ्‍च दुरुपपादञ्‍च विसम्वादकञ्‍चासम्बद्धञ्‍चचेति न विदुषां
children.translated_text: All this is excessively laborious, difficult to establish, contradictory, and incoherent, and thus does not please the learned — this is what we say here.

If [one asks]: how is there positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) with the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)? We do not say with that very [particular], but with another particular of the same class (<s>tajjātīya</s>). And thus it has been said:

children.text: मणिप्रभायां मणिज्ञानं न प्रमाणं सत्यार्थाजनितत्वान्‍न प्रत्यक्षं । नाप्यनुमानं
तल्लक्षणाभावात् । यो हि यल्लक्षणहीनः स तेन रूपेण व्यवह्रियते यथा गौर्वाजिरू
children.translated_text: is treated as that [thing only improperly] — as a cow [is improperly called] a horse —
this is well-established.
Inference is the cognition of the inferable (<s>anumeya</s>) from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that is ascertained and possesses the three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>).
Here, in this case,
there is no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>).

children.text: न हि या या प्रभा सा सर्वा मणिरित्यन्वयः सिद्ध‍्यति
children.translated_text: For the positive concomitance that 'whatever light there is, all of that is a gem' cannot be established.
Nor is there negative concomitance
(<s>vyatireka</s>):

children.text: यो मणिर्न भवति स प्रभापि न भवतीति । व्याप्यव्यापकभावासिद्धेः ।
children.translated_text: that 'what is not a gem is also not a light.' Because the relation of pervaded and pervader (<s>vyāpya-vyāpaka</s>) is not established.

children.text: नापि पक्षत्वं मण्याकारज्ञानस्य प्रभाजनितस्य मिथ्यात्वात् । न चागृहीत
children.translated_text: Nor does the gem-shaped cognition produced by the light have the status of a thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), since it is false. And one who has not grasped the connection

children.text: सम्बन्धो लिङ्गादनुमेयं प्रत्येति । योप्यविधानेन द्रागेव प्रत्येति स पूर्वमेव गृहीत
children.translated_text: does not cognize the inferable from the mark. Even one who cognizes quickly without [explicit] procedure has previously grasped the connection

and apprehends the inferable from the mark; otherwise apprehension would be impossible. Nor does the light of a gem appear as an effect of the gem in the way that smoke is [an effect] of fire, since [the light]

children.text: कार्यत्वेन मणेः प्रभा प्रतिभासते कारणरूपेणैव तस्याः प्रतिभासनाज्ज्ञापकत्वाच्‍च
children.translated_text: appears in the form of the cause itself and is [merely] an indicator.
A logical mark must be ascertained, not unascertained, like doubtful smoke.
And here there is no ascertainment,
since it is a false cognition.

The cognition of a gem in gem-light is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>: not perception, since it is not produced by a real object; nor inference, since it lacks the definition thereof. For one who lacks the defining characteristics of something

children.text: प्रभायामभ्रान्तमेव चक्षुर्विज्ञानमादौ जायते तेन कार्यत्वं प्रभाया
children.translated_text: that in the light, a non-erroneous visual cognition first arises, and through that the effect-nature of the light
is ascertained —
this is extremely rash. This is itself a sensory cognition which, due to its vividness, like a cognition affected by passion,
arises erroneously due to defects in the sense organ, etc., apprehending the light as having the form of a gem without discrimination.
And in that case, the aspect of light
is not cognized.
And what is not cognized in its aspect cannot be the object of apprehension, for otherwise everything would be the object of apprehension for everyone.
And this is not

children.text: मानसी भ्रान्तिरिन्द्रियदोषनिवृत्तौ पुनः स्वरूपेणैव विषयग्रहणात् । न च तादात्म्य
children.translated_text: a mental error, since upon the removal of the sensory defect, the object is again grasped in its true form. Nor is there a relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) between the gem and the light, since they are different. And the object, when apprehended, determines the cognition's validity or invalidity.

children.text: प्रतिबन्धो मणिप्रभयोर्भेदात् विषयो चाधिगते ज्ञानस्य प्रमाणाप्रमाणत्वञ्‍चेति ।

children.translated_text: As for what was said —

children.text: तेन हि निर्विषया कस्यचित्प्रवृत्तिरस्त्यत्र च मणिज्ञानं प्रभाविषयं
children.translated_text: By that, someone's activity may be without an object. But here the gem-cognition has the light as its object,

children.text: न च प्रभा मणिर्येन यथाध्यवसायं प्रवर्त्तमानः स कृती स्यात् । अनुमानन्तु लिङ्गरू
children.translated_text: and the light is not a gem, so one acting in accordance with [such] determination would not be successful. Inference, however, does not deviate from the nature of the logical mark.
And because it [the gem-cognition] is produced by what is not the [actual] object, it is a false cognition. But erroneous [inference], through its universal aspect —

children.text: विजातीयव्यावृत्तरूपता हि वस्तुनः स्थितैवान्यथा विजातीयतद्रूपमपि तद्वस्तु
children.translated_text: for the nature of a thing as excluded from dissimilar things is well-established; otherwise, even what has the form of a dissimilar thing would be that thing —

children.text: स्यादिति तदाकारो वस्तुसन्धायी । प्रभायान्तु न मणिरूपता विजातीयव्यावृत्त
children.translated_text: therefore that aspect is in contact with reality. But in the light, the form of a gem as excluded from dissimilar things
does not exist, since [the cognition] has only light as its object.
But inference, through having the aspect of the inferable, has contact with reality.

children.text: सति प्रतिबन्धे प्रामाण्यं प्रभायान्तु मणिज्ञानं नैवमिति नेदमनुमानम्
children.translated_text: Where there is a real connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), there is validity. But the gem-cognition in the light is not like this — therefore this is not inference.
For this very reason,
that even something of this kind is non-deceptive, yet in ultimate truth it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all,
being
it is used as an illustration, being outside the thesis accepted by both proponent and opponent, in order to demonstrate the supreme greatness of [real] connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) —
a thoroughly false cognition. Therefore the author of the treatise (<s>śāstrakāra</s>) says:
"Even though there is no difference in being false cognition, there is a difference with respect to efficacious action (<s>arthakriyā</s>)."

children.text: एतदेव व्याचष्‍टे । अत्र हि मिथ्याज्ञानात्प्रदीपप्रभायां मणिरूपेण ग्रहणान्‍नेदं

children.translated_text: the light of a lamp seen through a hole in a skull-cup or a keyhole.
Having restated the falseness, he states the negative concomitance:
(<s>arthakriyā</s>)."
"A difference with respect to efficacious action

The word 'api' (even) here is in the sense of emphasis. Thus, transgressing the words of the treatise-author and reason, the attempt to establish validity [of gem-cognition] merely reveals deception — therefore one should desist from this worthless investigation.

He explains this very point: Here, this [gem-cognition] arising from false cognition — from grasping as a gem in the light of a lamp — is not distinguished [from other false cognitions], but is itself merely a false cognition, like the cognition of a gem in
Even so, when there is concordance, the non-deceptiveness of inference is all the more [established].
Although there is no arising of unprecedented beings, and <s>Buddhas</s> are infinite in the three times, nevertheless
there is no exhaustion of <s>saṃsāra</s> — just as there is no end to space and infinity. Because in each direction, the stream of beings is endless.
Even one whose mind has gone elsewhere sees form with the eye;
the non-apprehension of the convention [associated] with that is clear there, and conceptualization arises from that.
Words denoting universals, and conceptualization having the same object as them —
in the absence of non-conceptual [perception], how is apprehension of the particular possible?
Those who have disregarded the meaning of reality, performing elephant-closing-the-eyes [i.e., willful ignorance],
extend their investigation of external [objects] merely through worldly understanding.

children.text: को वा विरोधो बहवः संजातातिशयाः पृथक् ।
children.translated_text: What contradiction is there if many [things], each having attained excellence separately,
were the cause of cognition, like the sense organs and so forth?
If [one objects:] how can what belongs to a different time be apprehended? — They know apprehension [to be possible].

children.text: आस्वाद्य कोपि लवणं जलमेकदेशे सर्वं तथेति लवणाम्भसि वेत्ति यद्वत् ।
children.translated_text: Just as someone, having tasted salt in one place of water, knows 'all [the water] is like that' regarding salt water,
so having ascertained smoke produced from kitchen fire, the discerning one understands 'all [smoke] is like that' through the three courses of reasoning.

children.text: येषु सत्सु भवत्येव यत्तेभ्यो ह्यस्य कल्पने ।
children.translated_text: From whichever [things], when present, something invariably arises —
if [those are posited as] causes, there would be infinite regress of causes everywhere.
Just as in a pot — an aggregate of form, smell, taste, and touch —
a subsequent determination arises in the visual [cognition] that grasps [only] form.
A superimposed determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) — having seen one [instance of] smoke, one determines all fire.

children.text: अनुपलम्भसहायेन प्रत्यक्षेण मयाग्‍निजन्मा धूमः परिच्छिन्‍न इति सकल

children.translated_text: instances excluded from everything other than that, by the cognition of the determination that arises in one possessing that [fire]. By visual cognition, only form is seen; by the subsequent conceptualization produced by its force,

children.text: र्विज्ञानेन रूपमात्रं दृष्‍टं तद्वलोत्पन्‍नपृष्‍ठजेन विकल्पेन रूपगन्धरसस्पर्शसमुदायो
children.translated_text: one determines: 'a pot — an aggregate of form, smell, taste, and touch — has been seen by me.' Where there is disagreement on this point, the practice of valid cognition would be destroyed.

children.text: घटो मया दृष्‍ट इत्यध्यवसीयते । अत्र विप्रतिपत्तौ प्रमाणव्यवहारोच्छेदः स्यात् ।
